from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        u_label = Tex("u", color=BLUE).next_to(u.get_end(), UP)
        v_label = Tex("v", color=RED).next_to(v.get_end(), DOWN)

        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        parallelogram = Polygon(

            np.array([1+2, 2-1, 1+0.5]), 
            np.array([2, -1, 0.5]), 
            color=PURPLE, fill_opacity=0.3
        )
        self.place_in_area(parallelogram, 'A4', 'C6', scale_factor=0.7)

        self.add(self.lecture[2])
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Geometric Intuition & Determinants", [
            "The cross product is a determinant.",
            "Zero area means vectors are collinear.",
            "It measures how independent vectors are."
        ])
        
        # Define objects
        parallelogram = Polygon([0, 0, 0], [1.5, 0.5, 0], [2.0, 2.0, 0], [0.5, 1.5, 0], 
                               fill_color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_width=2)
        
        formula = MathTex(r"|\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}| = \det\begin{pmatrix} a_x & b_x \\ a_y & b_y \end{pmatrix}", font_size=32)
        
        # Asset: Right-hand rule icon
        hand_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/hand.svg")

        # Group for positioning as per Issue 34
        content_group = VGroup(parallelogram, formula)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_in_area(content_group, 'B3', 'E5', scale_factor=0.85)
        self.play(Create(parallelogram))
        self.play(Write(formula))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        flat_parallelogram = Polygon([0, 0, 0], [1.5, 0.5, 0], [0, 0, 0], [0, 0, 0], 
                                     fill_color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.1)
        self.play(Transform(parallelogram, flat_parallelogram), run_time=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Place hand icon using constraints
        self.place_at_grid(hand_icon, 'E2', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(hand_icon))
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: The Geometric Intuition of the Cross Product

sections.title: Prerequisites: Vectors in 3D Space
sections.content: Briefly define vectors as directed segments in 3D space. Introduce the concept of a 'parallelogram' spanned by two vectors, u and v, as the geometric foundation for the cross product.
sections.example: Imagine two robotic arms positioned at the origin, pointing in different directions; the space between them represents the 'tent' or parallelogram we aim to measure.

sections.title: Definition of the Cross Product
sections.content: Introduce the cross product result as a vector perpendicular to the original plane. Use the Right-Hand Rule to determine the direction. Emphasize that the magnitude equals the area of the parallelogram formed by the two input vectors.
sections.example: A spinning propeller blade: the vectors follow the blade, while the cross-product vector points straight out along the axle, indicating the axis of rotation.

sections.title: Geometric Intuition & Determinants
sections.content: Visualize the cross product as a determinant calculation. Explain that if the area (determinant) is zero, the vectors are collinear (overlapping). This provides a intuitive measure of 'how parallel' or 'how independent' vectors are.
sections.example: A digital artist using a 3D modeling tool: dragging two vectors—if they are perfectly aligned, the cross product vanishes, signaling the 'collapse' of the 3D surface area.

sections.title: Linear Transformations and Orientation
sections.content: Explain the cross product as a linear transformation where the input vectors are mapped to a new space. Discuss how the cross product preserves (or flips) the orientation (handedness) of the coordinate system.
sections.example: A character in a video game moving through a portal: the cross product helps calculate the surface normal, ensuring the character walks on the ground rather than falling through the wall.

sections.title: Summary & Application
sections.content: Recap: Cross product = Perpendicular vector + Area calculation. Connect this to real-world physics, such as torque (force x lever arm) which is the classic application of this geometric relationship.
sections.example: An animation of a wrench tightening a bolt: the 'force' vector and 'lever arm' vector combine via cross product to show the resulting torque vector moving the bolt forward.
